trust_decision.summary: i_readraw_wiol accepts the caller-supplied raw_datachannels without a range check and sizes the per-line input buffer as xsize*datachannels without an overflow check; an out-of-range value gives a huge size_t and mymalloc exit()s the process.

landing_point.why: The summary names i_readraw_wiol and raw_datachannels. The function sits in the single raw.c file, and its existing storechannels range check (raw.c:80-83) is the obvious template to copy.

fix_sites.entry_point: Imager->read(type => 'raw', raw_datachannels|datachannels => N) (Imager.pm:1725-1745); also the exported XS function Imager::i_readraw_wiol (Imager.xs:3023-3029, Imager.pm:72)
fix_sites.module_kind: format decoder (C core, raw image reader)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The only lower-level route (XS i_readraw_wiol, Imager.xs:3023) calls the same C function, so the in-function fix covers it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: There is no O2 site or O8 route to dismiss. The best a solver could argue is that raw_datachannels is a trusted caller option, not file data, so validating it is a usability nicety.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: datachannels larger than storechannels (e.g. 4 read into 3, dropping junk), datachannels smaller than storechannels (zero-filled extra channels), and datachannels up to 16 (the fix's test reads 16) must keep working. A fix that caps datachannels at 4 (MAXCHANNELS), or requires it to equal storechannels, breaks the documented use.

O6_input_shapes: legacy option spelling 'datachannels' that maps to the same parameter (Imager.pm:1737)

O7_producer.where: The value comes straight from the read() options (Imager.pm:1737); no schema, serializer, cache or config loader is involved.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: exbuflen = im->xsize*storechannels computed without im_mult_overflow2, next to the fixed inbuflen
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It mirrors the inbuflen line. A maintainer could rely on the image-creation check, but a planted variant with a wider storechannels range would be a believable miss. It is still a WHERE-type sibling in the same function.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted second raw entry (e.g. an i_readraw_multi or a 16-bit raw variant in another file) that takes datachannels without the new range check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Raw readers for higher bit depths are a natural extension (the comment at raw.c:151-152 already anticipates higher-bit raw). It would be a second implementation, but it is synthetic, not in the real code.

O9_family: Integer overflow / unchecked caller-supplied size leading to an allocation-failure process exit (CWE-190/CWE-789)

O10_build.toolchain: perl, ExtUtils::MakeMaker, C compiler (perl Makefile.PL && make)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add 'if (datachannels < 1 || datachannels > 4)' modelled on the storechannels check: this closes the exit but rejects the legitimate 5..16 datachannels.

out_of_scope_notes: Other decoders size line buffers as width*sizeof(...) (pnm.c:152, tga.c:813, PNG/impng.c:466). These widths are already bounded by image creation (img8.c:176) and are not the raw datachannels protection, so they were not pursued.
The fix also swaps i_img_empty_ch for i_img_8_new (fix.diff:89). This is behaviour-neutral: img8.c:101-107 just calls im_img_empty_ch.
unverified: repo_mb not measured (no shell size check run); Imager with bundled format modules is likely 5-30 MB.
What exactly happens for datachannels == 0 before the fix (malloc(0) may return non-NULL, so the read may succeed rather than exit) was not traced at runtime.
Present-in-latest is not applicable (no latest release supplied); O8 is empty.
